title: Fixed-Point Bifurcations and Path-Information Bounds in Nonlinear Exceptional-Point Sensing
abstract: Nonlinear exceptional points (NEPs) were proposed to circumvent the noise--responsivity cancellation that limits linear exceptional-point sensors. At an NEP, the stationary frequency response can be singular while the Hamiltonian Petermann factor remains finite, suggesting a genuine signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) enhancement. Yet recent model-specific analyses of nonlinear fluctuations have reached conflicting conclusions. We prove that any singular stationary frequency response requires a fixed-point bifurcation of the nonlinear dynamics. In local fluctuation regimes, the singularities in responsivity and long-time frequency uncertainty are both set by the critical relaxation rate, leading to exact cancellation in the SNR and precluding any divergent enhancement. Furthermore, we derive a path-information bound that applies across both local and nonlinear fluctuation regimes and places a finite ceiling on the long-time SNR enhancement. Notably, this upper bound is attainable in the local fluctuation regime, implying that frequency readout under such parameter settings is information-optimal.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes nonlinear exceptional-point sensing, proving that while the response can appear singular, the achievable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is fundamentally limited. By deriving a path-information bound, the authors show that the apparent infinite enhancement is impossible, establishing a finite, information-optimal ceiling for sensing performance.
main_problem: The paper addresses conflicting theoretical conclusions regarding the achievable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) enhancement in nonlinear exceptional-point (NEP) sensing.
main_result: It proves that any singular frequency response requires a fixed-point bifurcation, and crucially, the SNR enhancement is fundamentally limited by a finite path-information bound, precluding divergent asymptotic gains.
method: The analysis employs the Coherent-Amplitude Matrix (CAM) representation to analyze phase-invariant dynamics, deriving fixed-point bifurcation conditions and applying path-information theory.
model_or_system: The study models nonlinear sensor systems (e.g., optical micro-cavities) whose dynamics are governed by stochastic Langevin equations, analyzed via a reduced center manifold flow.
key_observables: Responsivity ($\mu_\omega$), frequency uncertainty ($\sigma_\omega$), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), and the path-information bound ($\dot{I}_{	ext{path}}$).
important_parameters: Critical relaxation rate ($\lambda_c$), bifurcation parameter ($\epsilon$), and the effective drive/coupling coefficients ($F_c, g_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a global U(1) phase symmetry allowing the use of the CAM representation, and it focuses on the local fluctuation regime (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the CAM representation transition from an annular to a localized distribution around a fixed point. Figure 2 likely details the scaling of responsivity and noise in the local fluctuation regime.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the mathematical requirement for singular response (fixed-point bifurcation) using the CAM formalism. It then analyzes the local fluctuation regime, showing the cancellation of divergent terms in the SNR. Finally, it derives and emphasizes the universal, finite path-information bound that governs the long-time sensitivity.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical constraints on quantum sensing, moving beyond simple scaling arguments to establish fundamental information-theoretic limits based on nonlinear dynamics and bifurcations, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems.
